newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool drop reverses earlier gain.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool drop reverses earlier gain.

text.p: Australian wool markets fell on Thursday in reaction to last week's strong gains and as buyers appeared to complete shipping orders, analysts said.
The eastern market indicator fell by 14 cents to 605 cents a kg clean on Thursday, Wool International reported.
This followed a day of sliding greasy wool futures prices and reversed strong gains posted in the wool auction market last week.
On Wednesday last week the eastern market indicator jumped by 28 cents to 612 cents a kg to post its best performance for some time.
The indicator went on to rise a further five cents to post a total 33 cent gain for the week -- the second selling week of the second half of the 1996/97 season ending June 30.
Brokers attributed the rise last week to tightness of supply, better fundamentals for wool and the shipping schedule needs of particular buyers.
A slight two cents gain at Wednesday's opening auction this week disguised the fact that the market was just hanging on, analysts said on Thursday.
The movement in quotes showed that the market was poised for a slide, even though offered volumes remained thin, they said.
Japan's Itochu remained a main buyer in the market but its purchases had slackened since last week, they said.

Greasy wool futures prices slid on the Sydney Futures Exchange on Thursday, with contracts down across the range. Price falls were between three cents for December 1997, to 790 cents a kg, to 20 cents for April 1997, to 715 cents a kg. Only December 1997's fall was limited to the single digit range.
Volume was moderate with 44 contracts traded.
